# Table

> Rows of the same kind of thing, side by side in columns, like the accounting app's payments. No box, a hairline between rows.

## Props

| `caption` | slot |  |  |
| `head` | slot |  |  |
| `rows` | slot |  |  |

## Anatomy

- `root`: A real `<table>`. It has no surface of its own: no box, no fill. The rows draw the lines.
- `caption` (optional): The `<caption>`, above the rows, lined up with the text in the first column.
- `head` (optional): The `<thead>`. Only there when `head` is.
- `body`: The `<tbody>` with the rows.

## When to use

- **Data read across.** Several things of the same kind with the same few facts each, read across: payments with a date, what they're for and an amount.
- **Columns that mean something.** When the columns mean something: an amount in the same place on every row, so the eye runs down them.

## When not to use

- **One fact each.** A list of things to pick or go to, one fact each. That's **ListItem**.
- **Laying out a page.** Laying out a page or a form. A table is for data.
- **Too many columns.** More columns than fit on a phone. Two or three is right: put the rest in the row's description, the way the accounting app puts "leaves €4,210" under the date.

## Behaviour

The table draws nothing itself. Each TableRow draws a hairline under it, the last one too, so the table has an end. Rows that are links or can be picked react to the pointer; the others don't.

## Accessibility

- **Element**: a `<table>` with a `<caption>`, a `<thead>` when there are column headers and a `<tbody>`. Each row's first cell is usually its header (`<th scope="row">`), so a screen reader names the row when it reads an amount.
- **Name**: the `caption`. Without one, an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` on the table.
- **Keyboard**: nothing of its own. A row that's a link or a button is one Tab stop, through its header cell.
- **Focus**: TableRow's focus ring, on the whole row.

## Content

A caption in sentence case, a few words. Column headers are one or two words.
